summary: The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 127 - 108, at Wells Fargo Center on Thursday evening. Both teams came out strong in the first quarter but the Bulls held the advantage, leading 41 - 38, heading into the second. However, the Sixers bounced back in the second, where they outscored the Bulls, 27 - 17, to take a 65 - 58 lead heading into halftime. The Sixers came out in domination mode in the third and outscored the Bulls, 37 - 18, to take a 102 - 76 lead heading into the fourth. The Bulls put up a fight in the fourth but the 76ers were able to cruise to their first win of the season without a problem. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 30 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting, in 33 minutes of action. Ben Simmons put up big numbers with 13 points, 13 rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and one steal, in 34 minutes. Robert Covington finished with 20 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block, in 29 minutes. The Sixers shot 48 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 30 points on 11 - of - 20 shooting, six rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes of action. Bobby Portis followed up with 20 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Antonio Blakeney added 15 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Bulls shot 44 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 33 from long range. The Bulls (0 - 1) look to bounce back as they play host to the Pistons on Saturday. The Sixers (1 - 1) play host to the 76ers on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 116 - 115, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The Magic jumped out to a quick 90 lead and went ahead to push it to a 26 - 10 advantage with 4:55 left in the first. However, the Sixers battled back and cut the gap to just two points, trailing, 32 - 30, after one. The 76ers pulled ahead in the second carried the lead for most of the quarter, before taking a 63 - 52 lead into halftime. The tides turned again in the third quarter, as the Magic outscored the 76ers by eight, to cut the deficit to three points, heading into the final frame. The Sixers maintained their edge and pushed the lead back to 10, with five minutes to go in the game, but the Magic used an 18 - 9 run to make it a one - point game with 5 seconds left and possession. The Magic were not able to convert on the final play and dropped their second game in as many nights. On the other hand, the Sixers earned their second straight win. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 32 points, 10 rebounds and three assists, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick came up huge in 32 minutes off the bench, with 31 points, four rebounds and four assists. Dario Saric finished with 13 points, nine rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal, while Robert Covington added 12 points, four rebounds, two steals, one block and one assist. The Sixers shot 48 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Evan Fournier was the high - point man for the Magic with 31 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Nikola Vucevic had a big night with 27 points, 13 rebounds, 12 assists and two steals, in 37 minutes of action, while Aaron Gordon finished with 20 points, 12 rebounds three assists, three blocks and one steal. The Magic shot 46 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 29 from distance. The Magic (1 - 2) take on the Celtics in Boston on Monday, while the 76ers, head to Detroit to challenge the Pistons on Tuesday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 105 - 103, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The battle of two evenly matched teams was as good as expected, as neither club gave an inch through four quarters. A see - saw first half saw the 76ers (3 - 3) enter halftime holding a slim 63 - 62 advantage. Ultimately, a standout defensive effort by Philadelphia that saw them limit the Hornets (3 - 4) to 18 points in the final period helped key the hard - fought win. Both teams scuffled from the field with Charlotte's 39 percent success rate only slightly exceeding the Sixers' 38 percent figure. However, the home squad enjoyed a strong rebounding advantage, winning the battle of the boards by a 56 - 48 margin. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with a game - high 37 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal. Miles Bridges followed with a bench - leading 14 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds and one steal. Cody Zeller produced 12 points, six boards and one steal, while Jeremy Lamb matched his point total and added three rebounds and one assist. Joel Embiid led the way for the Sixers with a 27 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and two blocks. Robert Covington generated an 18 - point, 10 - rebound double - double of his own. J.J. Redick poured in 15 point to lead the second unit. Ben Simmons supplied 14 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dario Saric contributed 11 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Markelle Fultz turned in 10 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Hornets head back home and await a visit from the Miami Heat on Tuesday night, while the 76ers remain home to take on the Atlanta Hawks on Monday evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 113 - 92, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday night. The 76ers (4 - 3) kept their undefeated run at home alive with a convincing win over the Hawks (2 - 4), as Atlanta fought hard but ultimately didn't have enough in them to battle with Philadelphia. In fact, Atlanta won the first quarter 25 - 20, but Philadelphia evened things up with a 27 - 22 second quarter that kept the score tied at 47 after the first two quarters. Philadelphia showed a bit of their playoff form last season with an impressive 31 - 13 third quarter, and they later closed things out with a 35 - 32 fourth quarter. Without a doubt, it was a strong showing from the Sixers and now they move up to 40 at home. Ben Simmons was the star of the game for Philadelphia and he came one assist short of a triple - double thanks to a 21 - point, 12 - rebound, nine - assist stat line, while Joel Embiid registered 10 points, six rebounds, six assists and two blocks. Markelle Fultz chipped in with 16 points and seven assists, Robert Covington added 11 points with six rebounds, and three bench players reached the 10 - point mark: J.J. Redick (14), Mike Muscala (14) and Landry Shamet (13). Kent Bazemore had 18 points to led all players for the Hawks, while rookie point guard Trae Young contributed with 11 points and eight assists. Dewayne Dedmon and Omari Spellman each chipped in with 11 points coming off the bench for the Hawks. All 13 Atlanta players scored, but only four reached the 10 - point mark.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 122 - 113, at Wells Fargo Center on Thursday evening. The Sixers got out to a solid start at home, as they held the upper hand for the entire first quarter, before taking a 34 - 30 lead into the second. They took off in the second, as they quickly pushed their lead to 10, and went on to outscore the Clippers by 11 in the quarter, to take a 72 - 57 lead into halftime. However, the Clippers came out strong in the third, as they kicked off the quarter with an 11 - 4 run, to cut the gap to eight. They kept battling and managed to trim the deficit to just four points, as they trailed 90 - 86 heading into the final frame. Despite the Clippers' strong push, the Sixers kept it together and managed to push their lead back to 11, less two minutes into the quarter. From there, the Clippers were only able to get within three points, as the 76ers went on to their fifth home win of the season. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 41 points, 13 rebounds, four blocks and one assist, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick followed up with 18 points, in 34 minutes off the bench, while Ben Simmons tallied 14 points, 11 assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Sixers shot 47 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, Lou Williams led the Clippers with 26 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting, in 24 minutes off the bench. Danilo Gallinari followed up with 25 points, eight rebounds and one assist, in 35 minutes, while Tobias Harris added 24 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block. The Clippers shot 44 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 23 from long range. The Clippers (4 - 4) will be right back in action, as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Friday. The 76ers (5 - 4) play host to the Pistons on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 109 - 99, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. Wire-to-wire wins are rare in today's NBA but that's just what the Sixers did here. In fact, Philly led by 24 points at times, as a 22 - point halftime lead was too much for the Clippers to overcome. Three-point shooting was key to victory, with Philly hitting 9 - of - 29 of their three's while holding Detroit to just 5 - of - 30 from long range. The free - throw shooting was also critical, as the Pistons connected on just 28 - of - 41 while the Sixers hit 44 - of - 51. Defense really carried Philly too, as they forced 17 turnovers from Detroit while holding them to under 40 percent from the field. The Pistons (4 - 4) had just one starter reach double figures in scoring, as Blake Griffin continued his magical season. In fact, he finished with 38 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and two steals on 12 - of - 21 shooting. Andre Drummond totaled eight points and nine boards. Langston Galloway led the bench with 13 points. The Sixers (6 - 4) got a spectacular performance out of Joel Embiid, as he tallied 39 points, 17 rebounds and two blocks on 10 - of - 18 from the field. Ben Simmons was second among starters, collecting nine points, five rebounds, five assists and five steals. J.J. Redick led the bench with 16 points and four assists. On deck for Philly is a road matchup versus the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday. As for Detroit, they host the Miami Heat on Monday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 133 - 132, in overtime at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (8 - 5) found themselves at the scene of the majority of their successes Friday, as they'd come into the contest with a perfect 60 record at home. After a nip - and - tuck first quarter, Philadelphia seemingly turned the game in their favor with a 32 - 17 advantage in the second period. To their credit, the Hornets (6 - 6) wouldn't go away, chipping away at their deficit until overcoming it in the fourth quarter. However after holding a five - point lead as late as the 1:18 mark of the final period, Charlotte allowed Philadelphia a 7 - 2 run at the end of regulation to force overtime. In a tightly contested extra period, a free throw apiece from Ben Simmons and Joel Embiid in the closing seconds helped create just enough cushion for the win. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with 30 points and added nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal. Jeremy Lamb provided 17 points, three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Dwayne Bacon supplied 15 points, one rebound, one assist and one steal. Willy Hernangomez delivered 14 points and four boards. Cody Zeller matched Hernangomez's scoring and rebounding totals, while Michael Kidd-Gilchrist generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double off the bench. Embiid led the Sixers with a 42 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Ben Simmons tallied a 22 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included eight boards, three blocks and two steals. Dario Saric contributed 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. J.J. Redick finished with 17 points, four assists and two rebounds. Markelle Fultz and Robert Covington started but only had seven points each. The Hornets remain on the road and take on the Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the 76ers pay a visit to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Utah Jazz, 113 - 107, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. It was a tale of two quarters in the first half for the 76ers (10 - 7), which exploded out of the gates for a 38 - point haul over the first 12 minutes. However, as prolific as Philadelphia was in the first quarter, they had as much trouble finding the net in the second. posting only 16 points. That was the extent of their scoring drought, though, as the home squad was able to outpace the Jazz (7 - 8) by a 59 - 55 margin in the second half. The game was not won without several scares in the final period, as Utah held a 107 - 105 lead as late as the 1:37 mark of the fourth quarter before the Big Three of Ben Simmons, Jimmy Butler and Joel Embiid notched the final six points to seal the win. Donovan Mitchell paced the Jazz with 31 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds, four steals and one block. Joe Ingles provided 14 points, two rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block. Ricky Rubio and Derrick Favors generated matching 13 - point efforts. Rudy Gobert contributed a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Butler paced the Sixers with 28 points, a total he supplemented with seven assists, three rebounds and two steals. Embiid delivered 23 points, seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks and two steals. J.J. Redick poured in 16 points. Simmons pitched in a full stat line of 10 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block. Amir Johnson led the second unit with 11 points. The Jazz remain on the road and pay a visit to the Boston Celtics on Saturday evening. The Sixers also hit the road and tangle with the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday night as well.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 119 - 114, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday evening. The 76ers (12 - 7) likely walked into Monday's home game feeling pretty good about themselves, and more specifically, their chances of cruising through an interconference contest against the struggling Suns (3 - 13), which had failed to win a road game in six tries. Philadelphia got an early wake - up call, as Phoenix jumped out to a 36 - 26 first - quarter lead. The visitors still held an advantage at halftime, albeit by just five points. The Sixers were able to eradicate their deficit in convincing fashion in the third and entered the final 12 minutes with a 92 - 86 edge. That would prove to be enough, although the Suns got as close 117 - 114 with 6 seconds remaining after a Mikal Bridges three - pointer. Phoenix kept the pressure on their hosts with a 51 percent success rate from the field, but they were outrebounded by a 53 - 31 margin. Devin Booker paced the Suns with 37 points, a total he supplemented with eight assists and three rebounds. T.J. Warren followed with 21 points, four rebounds, four assists and one block. Deandre Ayton posted 17 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. Bridges finished with 13 points, while Trevor Ariza filled out the stat sheet with 10 points, seven rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block. Richaun Holmes matched Ariza's point total while leading the bench. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with a 33 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, three steals and one block. Ben Simmons had a near triple - double with 19 points, 11 rebounds, nine assists and one steal. Mike Muscala matched Simmons' point total to lead the second unit. J.J. Redick poured in 17 points and added four rebounds and three assists. Jimmy Butler contributed 16 points, three rebounds, one assist and two steals. The Suns remain on the road and visit the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday'night, while the Sixers remain home and face the New Orleans Pelicans on that same evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 121 - 120, at Wells Fargo Center on Wednesday evening. The 76ers got out to a great start at home, as they outscored the Pelicans, 38 - 23, in the first quarter. The Pelicans made a push to start the second and quickly cut the gap to just three points. However, the home team was able to withstand, as the Sixers built their lead back up to double digits, and took a 67 - 57 lead into halftime. The third quarter was evenly matched, as neither team gave up any ground. The Pelicans led 96 - 87 heading into the final frame. The 76ers pushed their lead to 15 early in the fourth, but the Pelicans did not break, as the rallied back to make it a one - point game, with one minute remaining. Despite the visitor's best effort, the 76ers managed to stay one step ahead in crunch time, to pull off the impressive, 121 - 120, home win. This marks the fourth straight win for Philly. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 31 points, 19 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, in 32 minutes. Ben Simmons followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and one steal, in 35 minutes. Jimmy Butler and J.J. Redick chipped in 13 points each. The Sixers shot 45 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Jrue Holiday and E'Twaun Moore poured in 30 points each for the Pelicans. Julius Randle came up large as well, with 22 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and one block, in 28 minutes off the bench. The Pelicans (10 - 8) will look to bounce back as they take on the Knicks in New York on Friday. The 76ers (13 - 7) play host to the Cavs on Friday.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the host Philadelphia 76ers, 121 - 112, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The Cavs got down to business right away, as they outscored the home team, 31 - 23, in the first quarter. The 76ers picked up the slack in the second and outscored the Cavs, 31 - 23, in the quarter, to tie the game at 54 heading into halftime. However, the Cavaliers would not back down, as they came out tough in the third and matched the Sixers bucket for bucket, before they emerged with a one - point lead heading into the final frame. The Cavs continued to play one step ahead of the home team 76ers, and managed to build an 11 - point lead with 4:37 left in the game. The Cavs held on from there to earn their first road win of the season, and hand the 76ers their first home loss of the season. Rodney Hood led the Cavs with 25 points on 10 - of - 20 shooting, four rebounds and one assist, in 39 minutes. Collin Sexton followed up with 23 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, while Tristan Thompson added 18 points, 13 rebounds and two steals, in 35 minutes. The Cavs shot 53 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 22 from long range. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 24 points, 12 rebounds and three assists, in 32 minutes. J.J. Redick tallied 23 points of his own, on 5 - of - 11 shooting, while Ben Simmons and Jimmy Butler tallied 22 points each. The Sixers shot 53 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 33 from long range. The 76ers (13 - 8) will look to bounce back as they take on the Nets in Brooklyn on Sunday. The Cavs (3 - 14) play host to the Rockets on Saturday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 117 - 91, at Wells Fargo Center on Wednesday. Philly came into this game as a sizable favorite and a wire - to - wire victory vindicates that notion. In fact, the Sixers rode a 41 - 27 first quarter to victory, as they held a double - digit lead from there. In addition, they led by at least 19 points for the entirety of the second half. Philadelphia dominated through shooting, as they connected on 54 percent from the field and 45 percent from three - point range while holding New York to just 35 percent from the field and 21 percent from long range. Much of that was attributed to the ball movement, with the Sixers out - assisting the Knicks, 34 - 14. The Knicks (7 - 16) had just three players reach double figures in scoring, as Enes Kanter led the way with 17 points and six boards. Mario Hezonja matched those 17 points, adding five rebounds and four steals to his tally. Damyean Dotson led the bench with 16 points, four rebounds and three steals. Tim Hardaway Jr. had a game to forget, as he scored five points on 1 - of - 11 shooting, as that one made shot was a layup. The Sixers (15 - 8) got another sparkling performance from Joel Embiid, as he collected 26 points, 14 rebounds and seven assists/. J.J. Redick accrued 24 points, two rebounds and two assists on 10 - of - 14 from the field. Ben Simmons tallied 14 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. Mike Muscala and Furknan Korkmaz both reached double figures in scoring off of the bench. On deck for Philadelphia is a home matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Friday. As for New York, they're off until Saturday when they welcome the Milwaukee Bucks to The Garden.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Washington Wizards, 123 - 98, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (16 - 8) set the tone early for what would be a comfortable victory, establishing a 31 - 19 first - quarter lead that had grown to 68 - 46 by halftime. Philadelphia had no trouble maintaining a sizable advantage in the second half over the reeling Wizards (8 - 14), who were playing without Otto Porter, Jr. (personal). The Sixers limited Washington to 40 percent shooting (including 29 percent from three - point range) while winning the rebounding battle by a 58 - 42 margin. Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 19 points. Austin Rivers followed with a bench - leading 15 points and also offered two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Thomas Bryant drew a start at center and posted 12 points, seven rebounds. one steal and one block. John Wall got off to a slow start and never recovered, tallying 11 points, seven assists, three rebounds and three steals. Philadelphia saw seven players hit double digits in the scoring column, with Joel Embiid leading the way. The big man posted a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks. T.J. McConnell was next with a bench - leading 15 points. J.J. Redick poured in 14 points. Ben Simmons managed a 13 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included eight rebounds. Furkan Korkmaz supplied 13 points, five assists, two rebounds and one steal. Landry Shamet turned in 12 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Mike Muscala matched Shamet's scoring total and pulled down 10 rebounds. Jimmy Butler collected 11 points, seven rebounds, four assists and four steals. The Wizards head back home and face the Brooklyn Nets on Saturday evening, while the Sixers remain home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Sunday evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 103 - 95, at Wells Fargo Center on Sunday evening. The Sixers got out to a quick, 10 - 3, lead but the Grizzlies stuck with it, leading to a, 26 - 25, advantage for the home team, after one quarter. The 76ers stayed on top in the second, where they outscored the Grizzlies, 28 - 19, to take a, 54 - 44, lead by halftime. Things tightened up again in the second half, as both teams matched each other for 24 points in the third quarter, leaving the Sixers ahead by 10 heading into the fourth. The Grizzlies started the fourth quarter with a quick 9 - 1 run, to make it a two - point game. However, the 76ers answered right back, pushing their lead back to nine, with five minutes left. The Grizzlies cut it as close as a four - point deficit, but could not do better than that, as the 76ers held on to earn their fourth straight win. J.J. Redick led Philly with 24 points on 9 - of - 17 shooting, in 30 minutes. Jimmy Butler tallied 21 points, three rebounds, two assists and a block. Ben Simmons finished with 19 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and two steals, while Joel Embiid added 15 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Meanwhile, Mike Conley led the Grizzlies with 21 points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Jaren Jackson Jr. followed up with 17 points, three rebounds, three blocks and a steal, while JaMychal Green tallied 14 points, seven rebounds and four steals. The Grizzlies (13 - 9) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Clippers on Tuesday. The 76ers (17 - 8) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Wednesday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 116 - 102, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday evening. The Pistons jumped to an early, 7 - 4, lead but the 76ers came back to tie it at 11, four minutes into the first quarter. The Sixers did not look back from there, as they used a quick, 90, run to create some separation, and held on to take a, 38 - 29, lead into the second quarter. The game slowed down in the second, as the Sixers and Pistons matched each other with 18 points in the quarter. Things picked up again in the third, where the Sixers held their nine - point lead for most of the quarter, until the Pistons finally made a run to cut the deficit to three, with under two minutes remaining. However, the 76ers charged back with a, 11 - 3, run to bring a, 87 - 76, lead into the final frame. The Pistons kept fighting and cut the gap to six early in the quarter, but the home team responded one final time, pushing the lead to 17 points with three minutes left in the contest. The 76ers cruised from there to their second win in a row, while the Pistons dropped their fifth in a row. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 24 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 32 minutes. Ben Simmons followed up with 18 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block, while T.J. McConnell added 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 28 minutes off the bench. Luke Kennard had a big night for the Pistons, with 28 points, eight rebounds and three assists, in 36 minutes. Blake Griffin (rest) did not suit up, but Andre Drummond finished with 21 points, 17 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal. The Pistons (13 - 12) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Wednesday. The 76ers (19 - 9) play host to the Nets on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 127 - 124, at Wells Fargo Center on Wednesday. The game was certainly not as close as the final score suggests, as the Nets were in control for nearly all of Wednesday's contest before the 76ers' second unit, led by rookie Landry Shamet scoring 10 points in the final minute of the game, made a late push but ultimately just ran out of time. The main reason Brooklyn found itself in full control of the outing was the stellar play of Spencer Dinwiddie, who scored a career - high 39 points in just 30 minutes off the bench. The point guard shot 4 - of - 6 from three and a11 - of - 18 from the field overall, but he did most of his damage from the free throw line, where he was 13 - of - 14. It was the fifth time this season the breakout 25 - year - old scored at least 25 points in a game. As for the rest of the Nets, Allen Crabbe was the high scorer out of the starters, posting 20 points while shooting 50 percent from the field. Joe Harris was 2 - of - 3 from behind the arc en route to scoring 14 points, while rookie Rodions Kurucs scored 13 points off the bench. As a team, the Nets were on fire from behind the arc, going 14 - of - 28 from deep. The 76ers had to play Wednesday's game without star guard Jimmy Butler (groin), and their star players certainly picked up some of the slack. Joel Embiid was a force down low, postig another massive double - double of 33 points and 17 rebounds in 38 minutes, while Ben Simmons had a terrific all - around performance with 22 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, four steals and two blocks. Lastly, Furkan Korkmaz, who started in Butler's absence, scored 18 points for the second straight night. Offensive production, however, wasn't the problem, as the 127 points the team gave up was the most Philadelphia allowed in nearly a month.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 113 - 101, at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The Pacers (19 - 10) fell behind by 10 points at the end of the first quarter, and given that the 76ers (19 - 11) had lost only twice all season on their home floor, things looked bleak for Indiana early. The visitors still trailed by 10 at halftime, but a prolific third quarter where they outscored Philadelphia by a 31 - 18 margin. The Pacers then kept the heat on in the fourth by adding nine points to their advantage and sealing a hard - fought road victory. Thaddeus Young led the Pacers by touching up one of his old squads for a 26 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and one block. Bojan Bogdanovic provided 18 points, five rebounds and two assists. Victor Oladipo, Domantas Sabonis and Cory Joseph generated matching 14 - point tallies. Oladipo added nine assists and three steals, Sabonis also pulled down 16 rebounds, Darren Collison mustered eight points but also dished out 10 assists. Joel Embiid paced the Sixers with a 40 - point, 21 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, one steal and one block. J.J. Redick contributed 22 points. Ben Simmons managed 18 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block. Furkan Korkmaz started for Jimmy Butler (groin) once again but only totaled six points and two rebounds. The Pacers head back home to face the New York Knicks on Sunday afternoon, while the Sixers pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Sunday afternoon as well.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the New York Knicks, 131 - 109, at Wells Fargo Center. The 76ers (21 - 12) entered this game losing three of their past four outings, but they bounced back in a huge way thanks to a 22 - point win playing in front of their crowd against a struggling Knicks (7 - 25) side that was unable to get things going from start to finish. As a result, New York have now lost 10 of their last 12 games. Philly established their terms early and jumped to a 38 - 33 lead after the first quarter. They would never looked back, though, and they actually won all quarters here. The final score per each quarter was: 38 - 33, 31 - 28, 30 - 24 and 32 - 24, respectively. Ben Simmons paved the way for the Sixers thanks to a triple - double of 13 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Joel Embiid was the top scorer with 24 points and he also added 10 rebounds. Jimmy Butler had a solid outing as well since he finished with 20 points, four rebounds and four assists. J. J. Redick had 14 points, and Landry Shamet delivered 17 points off the bench. Every Sixers player that saw action scored at least two points. Tim Hardaway Jr. was New York's top scorer with 27 points and he also added five assists. Kevin Knox had one of his best games as a pro and finished with 21 points and six rebounds, while Enes Kanter chipped in with 15 points and six boards. Emmanuel Mudiay filled the stat sheet thanks to 11 points, five assists and three boards. Damyean Dotson contributed 14 points off the bench.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 126 - 101, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. While there were 13 ties and 13 lead changes in the first half, Philadelphia held the lead for the entirety of the second half. In fact, the Sixers outscored the Raptors, 97 - 71, across the final three quarters to take control. The shooting disparity was key, with Philadelphia hitting 54 percent from the field and 33 percent from three - point range while holding Toronto to 39 percent from the field and 25 percent from long range. Ball movement played a huge factor in that, with the Sixers out - assisting the Raptors, 33 - 17. Defensive rebounding was also decisive, with Philly winning that battle, 49 - 33 The Raptors (25 - 10) decided to rest Kawhi Leonard for this game and it clearly hampered them in this defeat. Pascal Siakam was their best player, as he led the way with 26 points, six rebounds and two assists. Kyle Lowry accumulated 20 points, six rebounds and five assists. Norman Powell led their bench with 13 points and four boards. The Sixers (22 - 12) got a spectacular performance from Joel Embiid, as he collected 27 points and 11 rebounds on 10 - of - 15 from the field. Ben Simmons was just as good, tallying 26 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists on 11 - of - 13 shooting. J.J. Redick amassed 22 points, three rebounds and five assists while Jimmy Butler finished with 12 points, seven rebounds, seven assists and three steals. On deck for Philly is a Christmas Day showdown against the Boston Celtics on Tuesday. As for Toronto, they travel to face the Miami Heat on Wednesday for their next fixture.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 106 - 100, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday. This final scoreline makes this game look closer than it actually was, as Philly dominated throughout. In fact, the Sixers won each of the first three quarters by at least three points apiece, as they led by 17 heading into the fourth quarter. Doug McDermott chipped in 14 points on 5 - of - 8 shooting, in 20 minutes off the bench, while Myles Turner added 11 points, four rebounds and one block. The Pacers shot 44 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 18 from long range. The Pacers (1 - 1) will be right back in action as they play host to the Nets on Saturday. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the New York Knicks, 124 - 113, at Fiserv Forum on Monday night. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 123 - 108, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday. Overall, it was just a poor shooting night from the 76ers, as while 32 percent from behind the arc is a decent mark, they hit just 41 percent of their shots overall and 70 percent of their attempts from the free throw line en route to their second straight loss.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Orlando Magic, 113 - 91, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Saturday evening. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 124 - 109, at BMO Harris Bradley Center on Monday evening. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Sacramento Kings, 144 - 109, at Fiserv Forum on Sunday afternoon. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Chicago Bulls, 116 - 113, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 129 - 115, at Fiserv Forum on Saturday afternoon. Nikola Vucevic delivered a 19 - point, 19 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Aaron Gordon produced 14 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. D.J. Robin Lopez followed with a bench - leading 14 points and also had four rebounds, two assists and one block. Justin Holiday posted an 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, one steal and one block. The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 119 - 94, at United Center on Wednesday. Minnesota won this game in wire - to - wire fashion, as a 29 - 18 first quarter really set the tone. They followed that up with a 31 - 19 second quarter, as the T'Wolves led by 31 points at times in the second half. Their defense was the difference, as they held the Bulls to 41 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range. Minnesota connected on 50 percent from the field and 34 percent from long range. Rebounding was also a big factor, with Minnesota outrebounding Chicago, 52 - 45. The Timberwolves (16 - 18) got another vintage performance from Derrick Rose, as he tallied 24 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Karl-Anthony Towns collected 20 points, 20 rebounds and four assists. Taj Gibson totaled 16 points, three rebounds and two assists. Tyus Jones led their bench with 13 points and five assists. The Bulls (9 - 26) got Zach Lavine back from an ankle injury, as he provided 28 points and two assists off the bench. Lauri Markkanen led the starters with 16 points and seven boards. Wendell Carter Jr. amassed 12 points, nine rebounds and two blocks. Kris Dunn flirted with a triple - double, as he accumulated nine points, eight rebounds and seven assists before fouling out. Justin Holiday had a game to forget, as he scored two points on 1 - of - 11 shooting. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Chicago traveling to face the stumbling Washington Wizards and Minnesota playing host to the struggling Atlanta Hawks.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Chicago Bulls,112 - 84, at United Center on Wednesday. It didn't take long for this game to get out of hand, as the Magic (17 - 20) opened up a 16 - point lead in the first quarter and didn't look back. They continued to pile it on from there behind the stellar play of their starting frontcourt. Nikola Vucevic played just 26 minutes in the outing, but he still managed to post 22 points and and 12 rebounds on 10 - of - 15 shooting from the field. Close behind was Aaron Gordon, who had a terrific all - around performance, scoring 18 points to go along with seven rebounds and nine assists in 37 minutes. As a team, the Magic managed to take advantage of a poor defense effort from the home team, shooting 42 percent from three and a scorching 58 percent from the field overall. As for the Bulls (10 - 28), this was their second straight loss and the second straight game they failed to score at least 90 points. It was another miserable shooting night for Chicago, as while they managed to shoot a decent mark from three (35 percent), they hit just seven shots from deep and still shot just 42 percent from the field overall. Zach LaVine was the lead scorer with only 16 points, while Lauri Markkanen and Kris Dunn scored just 14 points each. What hurt the Bulls immensely was getting absolutely nothing out of starting center Wendell Carter Jr., as the rookie shot 0 - of - 5 from the field and posted zero points and one rebound in just 13 minutes.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 119 - 116, in overtime at United Center on Friday evening. The Bulls got out to a great start at home with a 30 - 18 lead after one quarter. However, the Pacers rallied in the second to cut the deficit to just four points by halftime. The third quarter was a bit quieter, as the Pacers outscored the Bulls 21 - 20 in the quarter. The Pacers continued to chip away through the fourth and took the lead mid way through the quarter, but the home squad did not give up and thanks to a clutch three - pointer from Zach LaVine, forced overtime. Victor Oladipo came up as the savior for Indiana, as the he drilled a last - second three in OT, to seal the win for the visitors. Oladipo led the Pacers with 36 points, seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and one block, in 37 minutes. Domantas Sabonis came up huge off the bench, with 23 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal, while Thaddeus Young finished with 16 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 31 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals, in 34 minutes. Lauri Markkanen finished with 27 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Wendell Carter Jr. added 15 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. The Bulls (10 - 29) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Sunday. The Pacers (26 - 12) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Sunday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Chicago Bulls, 117 - 100, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The Nets (20 - 21) came out ready to roll in enemy territory, building a 28 - 21 first - quarter lead. The two teams then alternated the advantage throughout the middle periods, but it was Brooklyn who carried the 88 - 82 lead into the final 12 minutes. They built on their edge from there, finishing the game on a 29 - 18 run to take home the double - digit victory. D'Angelo Russell led the way for the Nets with 28 points, supplementing them with five assists, four rebounds and one steal. DeMarre Carroll followed with 20 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. Jarrett Allen contributed 19 points, six rebounds and two blocks. Shabazz Napier registered 18 points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Jared Dudley supplied 10 points, four assists and one steal. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 27 points and added two rebounds, two assists and one block. Bobby Portis delivered 17 points and five rebounds. Kris Dunn managed 16 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen totaled 14 points, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Chandler Hutchison collected eight points, four rebounds and one assist. Wendell Carter, Jr. offered six points, eight rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. The Nets remain on the road and visit the Boston Celtics on Monday evening, while the Bulls take on the Portland Trail Blazers out west on Wednesday night.

The Miami Heat defeated the Chicago Bulls, 117 - 103, at United Center on Saturday evening. The Heat (22 - 22) walked into a hornet's nest despite the Bulls' unsightly 10 - 36 record, as Chicago came out ready to defend home court. Miami faced a slim 57 - 55 halftime deficit, but they came out of intermission ready to take control. The visitors outscored their hosts by a 62 - 46 in the second half to eventually secure the double - digit victory, The Heat shot an outstanding 57 percent, and the Miami second unit scored 64 of the team's points. Josh Richardson returned from a one - game absence due to an illness to lead the way with 26 points. He added three rebounds and two assists. Dion Waiters tallied 21 points, six boards and two assists. Tyler Johnson and Dwyane Wade managed matching 14 - point efforts. Wade added 10 rebounds and seven assists. Justise Winslow supplied 11 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. James Johnson generated 10 points, three boards, two assists and one steal. Hassan Whiteside offered six points but hauled in 10 rebounds, dished out three assists and recorded three blocks. Zach LaVine paced the Bulls with 22 points, adding six assists, three rebounds and one steal. Bobby Portis followed with 21 points and also posted six boards, two assists and one steal. Lauri Markkanen followed with 20 points, nine rebounds, two steals and one block. Jabari Parker delivered 11 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Heat remain on the road and face the Boston Celtics on Monday evening, while the Bulls pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday afternoon.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 121 - 101, at United Center on Wednesday. Atlanta hasn't had many dominant wins this season but this was a much needed wire - to - wire victory for them. In fact, a 42 - 25 first quarter really set the tone, as they held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Rebounding was key for the Hawks, as they outrebounded the Bulls, 51 - 37. Ball movement was huge as well, with Atlanta out - assisting Chicago, 31 - 20. The Hawks ended up shooting 50 percent from the field while holding the Bulls to 44 percent shooting. The Hawks (15 - 32) got a career - best 35 points from John Collins, adding eight rebounds, two assists and two steals to his tally on 14 - of - 16 from the field. Taurean Prince totaled 15 points, six rebounds and two assists. Dewayne Dedmon amassed 14 points, seven rebounds and five assists while Trae Young led the team with 12 assists despite going 1 - of - 12 from the field. Alex Len recorded a double - double off the bench. The Bulls (11 - 37) were led by Zach LaVine, as he collected 23 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Lauri Markkanen amassed 22 points and six rebounds. Kris Dunn accumulated 16 points, four rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks while Wayne Selden led the bench with 11 points. Chicago returns to action on Friday, as they play host to the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Atlanta, they travel to face the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday for their next fixture.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 106 - 101, at United Center on Friday. There were six ties and eight lead changes in this competitive game, as it came down to the wire. Los Angeles did most of their damage in the first and fourth quarters, outscoring Chicago, 53 - 39. The Clippers defense was key, as they held the Bulls to 39 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range. Ball movement was huge as well, with Los Angeles out - assisting Chicago, 27 - 20. The Clippers were much more effective with the whistle too, as they hit 22 - of - 29 of their free throws while the Bulls connected on 11 - of - 12. The Clippers bench was also a huge factor, outscoring the Bulls bench, 54 - 20; The Clippers (27 - 22) got a triple - double from Lou Williams off the bench, as he provided 31 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Tobias Harris led the starters with 29 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Avery Bradley totaled 11 points, five rebounds and two assists while Montrezl Harrell amassed 11 points and four rebounds off the bench. The Bulls (11 - 38) were led by Zach LaVine, as he tallied 29 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Bobby Portis started and finished with 18 points and 14 rebounds. Chandler Hutchinson accrued 12 points, 12 rebounds and two assists while Kris Dunn finished with nine points, four rebounds, 10 assists and four steals. Jabari Parker led the bench with 15 points, four rebounds and three assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Los Angeles playing host to the Sacramento Kings and Chicago welcoming the Cleveland Cavaliers to United Center.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 104 - 101, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The Cavaliers (10 - 41) finally reached the double - digit win mark in a tough contest on the road against the Bulls (11 - 39), as both struggling sides locked horns but ended delivering a tightly - contested affair that was only decided in the final minutes. Chicago won the first quarter by a two - point margin (29 - 27) and they held that lead at half time (53 - 51), but Cleveland turned things around. They won the remaining two quarters by slim margins as well (28 - 26 and 25 - 22, respectively) to walk away with a huge win away from home. Five Cleveland players reached the 10 - point mark in this game and their best scorer was Jordan Clarkson, who came off the bench to finish with 18 points, seven rebounds and six assists in only 22 minutes of action. Matthew Dellavedova also chipped in with 16 points and five assists in 22 minutes off the bench. As for the starters, Alec Burks had 18 points, Rodney Hood chipped in with 17, and Cedi Osman added 17 points with eight boards. Only four Chicago players scored in double digits and all of them were part of the starting lineup. The top scorer was Lauri Markkanen, as he contributed 21 points and 15 rebounds to the losing cause. Zach LaVine posted an oddly - similar stat line since he finished with 17 points and 12 boards. Wayne Selden had 15 points, and Robin Lopez added 16 points.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 125 - 120, at United Center on Wednesday. This was a tale of two halves, as Chicago dominated the first half but New Orleans prevailed in the second half. In fact, the Bulls led for the entirety of the first half while the Pelicans led for the final 16 minutes of action. A 27 - 17 third quarter really made the difference, as Chicago couldn't recover from that. Rebounding was key for New Orleans, as they outrebounded Chicago, 46 - 36. The shooting disparity was also key, with the Pelicans shooting 53 percent from the field and the Bulls hitting 49 percent of their shots. They also outscored Chicago in the paint, 60 - 50, while outscoring their bench, 63 - 27. The Pelicans (24 - 31) were led by Julius Randle, as he provided 31 points, seven rebounds and three assists off the bench. Jrue Holiday led the starters with 18 points, six rebounds and 11 assists. The Bulls (12 - 42) were led by Lauri Markkanen, as he finished with 30 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Zach LaVine accumulated 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and two blocks. Kris Dunn collected 18 points, four rebounds, eight assists and two steals while Robin Lopez generated 11 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Friday, with New Orleans playing host to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Chicago traveling to face the surging Brooklyn Nets.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 134 - 125, at Capital One Arena on Saturday. These teams made a huge move at the trade deadline on Thursday, as many of those pieces were huge factors here. Washington got the better of Chicago thanks to a 42 - 29 second quarter, as the Wizards led by at least six points for the entirety of the second half. The Wizards offense was unstoppable, as they shot 58 percent from the field and 44 percent from three - point range while holding Chicago to 50 percent from the field and 25 percent from long range. Much of that can be attributed to ball movement, with the Wizards out - assisting the Bulls, 38 - 28. Bench production was also critical, with Washington outscoring Chicago's bench, 64 - 38. The Wizards (24 - 32) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 31 points, two rebounds, four assists and four steals. Trevor Ariza accumulated 19 points, four rebounds and four assists. Tomas Satoransky finished with seven points, seven rebounds and 11 assists. Jabari Parker led the bench with 20 points, five rebounds and six assists. Bobby Portis also played well off the bench, amassing 10 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. The Bulls (13 - 43) were led by Zach LaVine, as he accrued 26 points, four rebounds and six assists. Lauri Markkanen finished with 20 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Otto Porter generated 17 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals while Robin Lopez totaled 18 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Wayne Selden Jr. led the bench with 17 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Chicago playing host to the surging Milwaukee Bucks and Washington traveling to face the Detroit Pistons.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 112 - 99, at United Center on Monday. Milwaukee came into this game as a sizable favorite and they won in workman - like fashion. In fact, they won or tied all four individual quarters, as a 62 - 50 second half really put separation between the two teams. That allowed Milwaukee to hold the lead for the final three quarters, as the Bucks finished the game on a 12 - 2 run to cap off the victory. The shooting disparity was key, with the Bucks shooting 48 percent from the field while holding the Bulls to 39 percent shooting. Rim protection was also critical, with Milwaukee out - blocking Chicago, 7 - 2. In addition, the Bucks outrebounded the Bulls on the defensive end, 44 - 36. The Bucks (42 - 14) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he tallied 29 points, 17 rebounds, eight assists and three blocks. Eric Bledsoe accrued 19 points, two assists and two steals. Malcolm Brogdon accrued 17 points, six rebounds and three assists while Khris Middleton collected 16 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals. The Bulls (13 - 44) were led by Zach LaVine, as he accumulated 27 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Lauri Markkanen amassed 20 points, 17 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Otto Porter totaled 18 points, seven rebounds and four assists while Robin Lopez finished with 17 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Chicago playing host to the Memphis Grizzlies and Milwaukee traveling to face the resurgent Indiana Pacers.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 122 - 110, at United Center on Wednesday evening. The hometown Bulls (14 - 44) got off to a surprisingly fast start against the typically defensive - minded Grizzlies (23 - 36), racking up 67 first - half points. However, given Chicago's defensive vulnerability, Memphis essentially kept pace, and the hosts' lead was only five at intermission. The Bulls kept coming in the third by adding another four points to their advantage, and a 13 - 7 run over the first 3:4 of the final period gave them the cushion they'd need for the double - digit home win. Chicago shot especially well and dominated on the boards, draining 56 percent of its attempts while outrebounding the visitors by a 47 - 31 margin. Avery Bradley put together a second straight productive outing by pacing the Grizzlies with 15 points. He added five assists, one rebound and one steal. Jaren Jackson, Jr., Mike Conley, Jonas Valanciunas and Delon Wright generated a quartet of 12 - point tallies. Bruno Caboclo and Joakim Noah had eight points apiece, with the former also supplying five rebounds and two assists, and the latter totaling three boards, three dimes and two blocks. Otto Porter, Jr. paced the Bulls with a career - high 37 points and supplemented them with 10 rebounds, two assists and one block. Robin Lopez furnished 25 points, five rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Lauri Markkanen generated a 21 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and one steal. Zach LaVine delivered 15 points, seven assists and six rebounds. Cristiano Felicio led the bench with eight points. Ryan Arcidiacono drew the start for Kris Dunn (back) and mustered just two points but also dished out 11 assists, hauled in six rebounds and recorded a steal. The Grizzlies are now off until Feb. 22, when they'll host the Los Angeles Clippers. The Bulls return to action that same night with a road matchup against the Orlando Magic.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Boston Celtics, 126 - 116, at United Center on Saturday night. The Bulls (16 - 44) were riding high after a hard - fought one - point road victory Friday against the Magic, but they had an exponentially difficult challenge just 24 hours later in the form of the Celtics (37 - 23). Matters looked a bit worrisome for Chicago early, as Boston forged a five - point lead after 12 minutes. However, the visitors never saw what hit them in the second, as the Bulls doubled them up by a 36 - 18 margin in the second to carry a 13 - point advantage into halftime. After both teams matched each other bucket for bucket in the third, the hosts put the final nail in the proverbial coffin with a 32 - point fourth quarter, ultimately allowing the Celtics to cut three points into their lead. Both teams shot well, but it was Chicago that dominated the boards with a 49 - 32 rebounding advantage. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 37 points, adding 10 assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Al Horford contributed 19 points, three assists, two rebounds and one block. Jaylen Brown registered 14 points, three rebounds and two steals. Jayson Tatum and Marcus Morris contributed 12 points apiece, with the latter notably hauling in six boards as well. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 42 points and supplemented them with six rebounds and four assists. Lauri Markkanen turned in 35 points, 15 rebounds, two assists and one steal. Robin Lopez collected 17 points, six boards and four assists. Wayne Selden saw extra playing time after Otto Porter, Jr. exited early with a leg injury, totaling nine points, six rebounds, two assists and one block. The Celtics remain on the road and next face off with their biggest Eastern Conference rival in the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday night. The Bulls remain home and tangle with the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 117 - 106, at United Center on Monday. Milwaukee came into this game as a sizable favorite and a double - digit victory vindicates that notion. Despite the fact that Chicago led by 13 points after the first quarter, Milwaukee responded with a 38 - 16 second quarter to take control. That allowed the Bucks to lead for the entirety of the second half, as Chicago never got it within a six - point margin in the third or fourth quarter. Rim protection was key for the Bucks, as they doubled up the Bulls in blocks, 6 - 3. Fastbreak scoring was also huge, with Milwaukee winning that battle, 15 - 5. The Bucks bench was also decisive, as they outscored the Bulls, 42 - 24 The Bucks (46 - 14) had to play without Giannis Antetounmpo (knee soreness) but this game was no problem. Khris Middleton led the way in his absence, as he tallied 22 points, four rebounds and three assists. Malcolm Brogdon accrued 22 points, two rebounds and five assists. Brook Lopez finished with 13 points, four rebounds and five blocks. The Bulls (16 - 45) were led by Robin Lopez, as he accumulated 26 points, three rebounds and two assists. Lauri Markkanen totaled 26 points, 12 rebounds and three assists. Timothe Luwawu-Cabbarrot started and accrued 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Zach LaVine collected 11 points, eight rebounds and nine assists. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Chicago traveling to face the Memphis Grizzlies and Milwaukee playing the Sacramento Kings on the road as well.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 123 - 118, at United Center on Sunday afternoon. The contest picked up where it left off in the Bulls' and Hawks' last meeting, which was four - overtime shootout. The first quarter was a high - scoring one, with the Hawks taking a 35 - 32 lead into the second. They managed to hold the edge through the second and pushed their lead to seven by halftime. The Hawks kept up the momentum in the third, as they pushed their lead to 15, just minutes into the quarter. However, the Bulls kept fighting and managed to cut the deficit to five by the start of the fourth. They played hard through the fourth as well, but the Hawks stayed in control and held on for the road win. Alex Len led the Hawks with 28 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two blocks, in 26 minutes. Trae Young followed up with 18 points, five assists and three rebounds, while Dewayne Dedmon added 13 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and one steal. The Hawks shot 47 percent from the field, including 21 - of - 43 from long range. Meanwhile, Lauri Markkanen led the Bulls with 19 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two steals, in 28 minutes. Robin Lopez followed up with 16 points, six rebounds, four assists and a block, while Kris Dunn chipped in 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. The Bulls shot 51 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 27 from long range. The Bulls (18 - 46) will look to bounce back as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Tuesday. The Hawks (22 - 42) take on the Heat in Miami on Monday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 108 - 107, at United Center on Wednesday evening. The 76ers got out to a good start on the road, with a 12 - 4 lead early on. However, the Bulls battled back to tie the score at 30 by the end of the first quarter. The contest stayed tight through the second, with neither team leading by more than a couple of possessions, until they sat tied at 57, entering halftime. The contest stayed close in the third. The Bulls led by one with a minute left in the quarter, but the Sixers closed strong, to take a four - point lead into the final frame. The Sixers pushed their lead to eight, four minutes into the fourth, but the Pelicans hung around, and managed to tie it up at 98, with 3:41 to go. The lead changed hands a few times in the final minute, before the Bulls came out on top, thanks to a game - winning bucket from Zach LaVine. LaVine led the Bulls with 39 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 36 minutes. Robin Lopez followed up with 19 points, nine rebounds and three assists, while Otto Porter Jr. added 15 points, nine rebounds, three assists and three steals. The Bulls shot 44 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 23 from deep. Meanwhile, Jimmy Butler led the 76ers with 22 points, four assists, three rebounds and three steals, in 35 minutes. Ben Simmons added 18 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists and four steals, while J.J. Redick added 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. The 76ers (41 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Rockets in Houston on Friday. The Bulls (19 - 47) play host to the Pistons on Friday.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Chicago Bulls, 112 - 104, at United Center on Friday evening. The Pistons (33 - 31) got themselves into a first - half hole, falling behind by a 66 - 49 halftime margin. The light went on at intermission, however, as Detroit held the Bulls (19 - 48) to just 14 third - quarter points and then racked up 43 over the final 12 minutes to secure the hard - fought road win. The visitors won the rebounding battle by a 41 - 35 margin, with Andre Drummond contributing 24 of those boards. Blake Griffin paced the Pistons with 27 points, adding three rebounds, three assists and one block. Reggie Jackson poured in 21 points and added two assists, one rebound and one steal. Drummond supplemented his outstanding work on the boards with 20 points, two assists, three steals and two blocks. Langston Galloway led the bench with 15 points, while Luke Kennard contributed 14. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 24 points and complemented them with six rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Otto Porter, Jr. supplied 23 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen turned in 18 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Robin Lopez furnished 13 points, four boards and one block. Kris Dunn totaled seven points, seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 28 minutes. The Pistons and Bulls next face off in a rematch in Detroit on Sunday afternoon.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 123 - 107, at United Center on Tuesday evening. The final score seemed especially improbable after one quarter, considering the Bulls (19 - 50) jumped out to a 34 - 16 lead through the first 12 minutes. However, the Lakers (31 - 36) began chipping away at their deficit in the second, shaving 13 points off Chicago's lead by halftime. The third quarter is when the game truly turned, as the visitors racked up a whopping 43 points during the period to erase the remaining deficit and build a 14 - point edge going into the fourth. Los Angeles ultimately cruised to a comfortable win, riding a red - hot 55 percent success rate from the floor to success. LeBron James led the Lakers with 36 points, complementing them with 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope supplied 24 points, six rebounds, one assist and two steals. Kyle Kuzma checked in with 21 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. Rajon Rondo generated a 14 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds and two steals. JaVale McGee delivered 10 points, 11 rebounds, three blocks and one steal. Reggie Bullock furnished nine points, two rebounds and two steals. Robin Lopez paced the Bulls with 20 points, adding seven rebounds and three assists. Otto Porter, Jr. delivered 19 points, nine rebounds and two assists. Kris Dunn contributed 18 points, nine assists and seven rebounds. Ryan Arcidiacono started for Zach LaVine (knee) and compiled 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Lauri Markkanen shot just 4 - for - 17 on his way to 11 points and five boards. The Lakers remain on the road and head north of the border to take on the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night, while the Bulls pay a visit to the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday evening.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Washington Wizards, 126 - 120, in overtime at United Center on Wednesday night. The Bulls (21 - 52) got off to a quick start by forging a 35 - 28 first - quarter lead, but the game was knotted at 60 by intermission. Fittingly, the game continued as a see - saw affair throughout the second half, and Bradley Beal sent the contest into overtime with a jumper at the 2 - second mark of the fourth period. However, Chicago opened the extra period on a 50 run and eventually outscored Washington by a 13 - 7 margin for the victory. Jabari Parker led the way for the Wizards with 28 points, adding six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Beal delivered 27 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks. Tomas Satoransky managed 16 points, seven assists, five rebounds and three steals. Bobby Portis posted 15 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Jeff Green provided 10 points, five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Trevor Ariza managed six points, two rebounds and two assists across 14 minutes before exiting with a groin injury. Lauri Markkanen paced the Bulls with 32 points, complementing them with 13 rebounds, five assists and one block. Kris Dunn turned in a 26 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included six rebounds and two steals. Shaquille Harrison registered 18 points, six rebounds and four steals. Cristiano Felicio totaled 15 points, six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot contributed 13 points, four boards, three assists and two steals. The Wizards head back home to face the Denver Nuggets on Thursday evening, while the Bulls remain home and take on the Utah Jazz at Saturday night.

The Utah Jazz defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 114 - 83, at United Center on Saturday. Utah came into this game as a sizable favorite and this final scoreline shows just why. A 33 - 18 first quarter really set the tone and then a 37 - 18 second quarter was the dagger. In fact, that allowed the Jazz to lead by at least 28 points for the entirety of the second half. Utah ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 34 percent from three - point range while holding Chicago to 36 percent from the field and 13 percent from long range. The Jazz also out - rebounded the Bulls, 57 - 44, and out - assisted them, 27 - 16. The Jazz (43 - 30) were led by Rudy Gobert, as he tallied 21 points, 14 rebounds, two assists and four blocks on 9 - of - 11 from the field. Donovan Mitchell finished with 16 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Joe Ingles accrued 13 points, six rebounds and three assists while Jae Crowder led the bench with 11 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Bulls (21 - 53) got a double - double from Lauri Markkanen to lead the team, as he amassed 18 points and 10 rebounds. Robin Lopez totaled 10 points and four boards. Shaquille Harrison collected six points, nine rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Cristiano Felicio led the bench with 10 points, six rebounds and two assists. On deck for Utah is a home matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Monday. As for Chicago, they're off until Tuesday when they travel to face the Toronto Raptors.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 118 - 98, at United Center on Wednesday. The Blazers (47 - 27) were widely expected to dominate the game against the Bulls (21 - 55) and that's exactly what happened at United Center, as they controlled the action right from tip - off. Portland quickly jumped to a 27 - 14 lead in the first half, and they would never relinquish that advantage. The second quarter finished 32 - 27 and the third one finished 28 - 24, so by the time of the final 12 minutes, Portland had the game already wrapped up. Chicago won the final quarter by a 33 - 31 score, but that didn't affect the score since Portland cruised their way to a 20 - point win. Six Portland players finished with a double - digit scoring total but surprisingly, Seth Curry led the way off the bench with 20 points. Rodney Hood had 15 points and Zach Collins added 13 points, meaning most of the heavy scoring was done thanks to the bench players. Damian Lillard finished with 11 points, seven assists and six rebounds. Enes Kanter delivered 13 points and six boards. Al-Farouq Aminu had 12 points and 11 boards. Ryan Arcidiacono chipped in with 12 points.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 124 - 101, at United Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with a few lead changes early on, before the Bulls emerged with a 28 - 26 lead after one quarter. However, the Raptors took over from there, outscoring the Bulls by 13, in the second quarter to take an 11 - point lead into halftime. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot tallied 18 points, 10 rebounds, two blocks and one assist, while Shaquille Harrison chipped in 15 points, eight rebounds, two assists, a block and a steal. The Bulls shot 42 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 30 from deep. The Bulls (21 - 56) will look to bounce back as they take on the Knicks in New York on Monday. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 116 - 96, at United Center on Saturday night. The 76ers (50 - 30) came into the contest looking to right their ship after forging a 2 - 5 record over the prior seven games. They had plenty going right on the offensive end during a 57 - point first half, Philadelphia then essentially sealed the win in the third with a stellar effort on both ends of the floor, as they outscored the Bulls (22 - 58) by a 29 - 19 margin during the period. JaKarr Sampson led the Bulls with 29 points, complementing them with eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot finished with 14 points, six rebounds, one steal and one block. Robin Lopez, Walter Lemon, Jr. and Shaquille Harrison turned in a trio of matching eight point efforts, with Lemon adding eight rebounds. The 76ers remain on the road and tangle with the Miami Heat on Tuesday night, while the Bulls remain home and face the New York Knicks on Tuesday evening.

The New York Knicks defeated the host Chicago Bulls, 96 - 86, at United Center on Tuesday. In a battle between two of the worst teams in the league, New York won in dominating fashion. In fact, they pulled out a wire - to - wire victory, leading by at least five points for the final three quarters.
