Shaquille Harrison accumulated 13 points, seven rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Robin Lopez generated 12 points, three rebounds and two blocks while Jakarr Sampson led the bench with 11 points and eight boards. Both teams play their finale on Wednesday, with New York playing host to the hungry Detroit Pistons and Chicago traveling to face the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 133 - 111, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday evening. This marked the first home game of the season for the Cavaliers, who started off with two tough road losses. The Cavs came out strong in quarter one, as they led 13 - 7 at the mid - way point and pushed it to a 10 - point, 34 - 24, lead heading into the second. However, the Hawks came to life in the second quarter, led by Trae Young, to outscore Cleveland, 40 - 26, in the frame and take a, 64 - 60, lead into halftime. The Hawks stayed on top through the third and held a six - point lead heading into the fourth. They kicked it to yet another gear in the fourth, where they jumped to a 17 - point lead mid way through the quarter. The Cavs could not keep up and were soon down by 20, en route to their third straight loss to start the season. Trae Young showed out with 35 points, 11 assists, two rebounds and one steal, in the best game of his young career. Alex Len was solid in the middle, with 16 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and four blocks, while Kent Bazemore tallied 23 points, five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. The Hawks shot 49 percent from the field, including 22 - of - 47 from long range. Jordan Clarkson was the high - point man for Cleveland, with 19 points, on 7 - of - 12 shooting, in 23 minutes off the bench. Kevin Love had a solid night with 16 points, 17 rebounds, three assists and one steal, while George Hill tallied 16 points on 7 - of - 9 shooting. The Cavs shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 27 from long range. The Cavs (0 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Wednesday. The Hawks (1 - 2) play host to the Mavericks on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 102 - 86, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday night. The Nets (2 - 2) and the Cavaliers (0 - 4) both entered this game with losing records, but it was clear from tip - off which team had it going tonight, and which hadn't it. Brooklyn jumped ahead with a 24 - 17 first - quarter lead, but the Cavaliers answered quickly with a 28 - 21 second quarter that evened things up 45 - 45 at the break. However, Brooklyn broke free in the third quarter and they never looked back after winning the third period with a huge 38 - 17 score. Cleveland would won the final 12 minutes by a 24 - 19 score, but it was too late for them. Brooklyn closed things out with ease and got back to .500, while the Cavs are still looking for their first win in their second post - LeBron era. All of the five Brooklyn starters scored in double digits. D'Angelo Russell led the way with an 18 - point, eight - assist effort, while Joe Harris chipped in with 16 points and six rebounds. Jared Dudley added 12 points, while both Caris LaVert and Jarrett Allen filled their respective stat sheets. LaVert finished with 10 points, six rebounds and four assists, while the center added 10 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Kevin Love ended being Cleveland's best player after finishing with 14 points and 11 rebounds across 28 minutes, and Rodney Hood added 10 points. Cedi Osman had eight points with six rebounds, but the biggest contributions came off the bench: Jordan Clarkson had 14 points, while the rookie Collin Sexton finished with 14 points of his own.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 119 - 107, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday. Cleveland came into this game winless and Indiana made sure to keep that going with this dominant win. In fact, the Pacers held the lead for the final 30 minutes of action, as they outscored the Cavaliers in the second and fourth quarters, 61 - 49. There were nine ties and 11 lead changes in the first 20 minutes though, as the other two quarters ended in deadlocks. Indiana's offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 65 percent of their shots while holding Cleveland to just 47 percent shooting. Ball movement was a huge part of that, with the Pacers out - assisting the Cavaliers, 28 - 21. The Pacers (4 - 2) were led by Bojan Bogdanovic, as he tallied 25 points, three rebounds and two assists on 10 - of - 14 shooting. Victor Oladipo finished with 24 points, three rebounds, six assists and three steals on 10 - of - 15 shooting. Darren Collison collected 15 points, two rebounds, six assists and three steals. Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 15 points and five boards. The Cavaliers (0 - 5) were led by Rodney Hood, as he totaled 17 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals. George Hill amassed 14 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Cedi Osman generated 10 points, four rebounds and three assists. Larry Nance Jr. led the bench with 15 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. On deck for Indiana is a home matchup versus the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday. As for Cleveland, they play host to the Atlanta Hawks on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 136 - 114, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday evening. The Cavaliers (1 - 6) finally won their first game of the 2018 - 19 season and they did it in emphatic fashion, as they didn't have problems to top the Hawks (2 - 5) in a game where they looked in absolute control right from tip - off. Cleveland quickly jumped ahead to a 35 - 31 lead after the first quarter, but Atlanta kept things close in the second as both teams went separated by one point (58 - 57) at the half - time break. The Cavs sealed the deal in the second half, though: they won the third quarter 41 - 30 and also won the final 12 minutes by a 37 - 27 score. Cleveland's second - half performance was, by far, the team's best performance across the entire season thus far. Seven players scored in double figures for the reigning Eastern Conference champions. Rodney Hood led the way with 26 points, while Cedi Osman chipped in with 20 points and five boards. George Hill added 17, Sam Dekker delivered 12 points with nine boards, and Tristan Thompson delivered a double - double of 11 points and 13 boards. Rookie Collin Sexton had 17 points and eight boards off the bench and Jordan Clarkson added 15 of his own. The Hawks only had four players scoring more than 10 points and the duo of Trae Young (24 points) and Alex Len (22 points, nine rebounds, two steals) led the way. Vince Carter did a good job of filling out the stat sheet since he contributed with 10 points, three rebounds and two assists in 24 minutes of action. Jeremy Lin came off the bench and chipped in with 12 points and eight assists in 24 minutes.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 110 - 91, at Quicken Loans Arena on Thursday. Denver came into this game as a sizable favorite and they showed why in this dominating performance. Despite the fact that the Cavaliers led by 12 points after the first quarter, the Nuggets dominated from there. In fact, Denver outscored Cleveland, 68 - 39, in the middle quarters, as they led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Bench production was the difference for the Nuggets, as they outscored the Cavaliers bench, 59 - 44. Rebounding was also huge for Denver, as they won that battle, 44 - 35. The Nuggets ended up shooting 48 percent from the field and 39 percent from three - point range while holding the Cavaliers to 41 percent from the field and 28 percent from long range. The Nuggets (7 - 1) starters weren't asked to do a whole lot, as Paul Millsap led them with 16 points and six boards. Juancho Hernangomez led the bench, as he provided 23 points, four rebounds and two blocks. Trey Lyles also played well off the bench, amassing 12 points and eight boards. Gary Harris finished with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. The Cavaliers (1 - 7) highest scorer came off the bench as well, with Jordan Clarkson totaling 17 points and three boards. Cedi Osman led the starters with 13 points and three rebounds. Tristan Thompson accrued 10 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Rodney Hood accumulated eight points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Denver welcoming the Utah Jazz to Pepsi Center and Cleveland traveling to play the Charlotte Hornets.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 95 - 86, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday night. The Thunder (6 - 4) had to deal with the absence of Russell Westbrook after he got injured on Monday against the New Orleans Pelicans, and they managed to dominate most of the contest against a Cavaliers (1 - 10) team that already reached double - digit losses through their first 11 games of the campaign. OKC jumped to a 23 - 20 lead in the first half, and increased their lead by eight points (48 - 40) by half time. Cleveland won the third quarter by one point (24 - 23) and it seemed they were on the rise heading into the final 12 minutes, but the Thunder closed things out with a 24 - 22 fourth quarter that pushed them two games over .500. No Westbrook meant no problem for the Thunder, as point guard Dennis Schroder led the way for OKC with 28 points and seven rebounds, but, oddly enough he didn't record a single assist despite starting as a point guard. Paul George filled the stat sheet thanks to 18 points, seven boards, two assists and two steals. Jerami Grant added 12 points with eight rebounds, and Steven Adams contributed with nine points, 13 rebounds and two blocks. Six Cleveland players scored in double digits and the leader was rookie Collin Sexton, who had 15 points. Tristan Thompson delivered a double - double of 10 points and 15 boards. J.R. Smith had 13 points, and Rodney Hood chipped in with 11 points, five boards and four assists. Jordan Clarkson had 11 points, nine rebounds and eight assists off the bench.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 113 - 89, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. This was easily the Cavaliers best performance of the season, as they held a double - digit lead for the final three quarters. Not only did they win all four individual quarters, a 38 - 23 first quarter really set the tone. Charlotte really killed themselves through long - range shooting, as they ended up going 8 - of - 41 from three - point range, missing 20 - straight at one point between the second and third quarters. The Cavaliers ended up shooting 53 percent from the field while holding the Hornets to just 35 percent shooting. Cleveland also hit 13 - of - 24 from long range while winning the rebounding battle, 60 - 37. The Hornets (7 - 7) got a nightmare performance out of Kemba Walker, as he tallied seven points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals on 2 - of - 16 from the field. Jeremy Lamb led the team with 22 points, six rebounds, two assists and three steals. Nicolas Batum was the only other player in double figures, as he totaled 11 points, five rebounds and three assists. The Cavaliers (2 - 11) were led by Jordan Clarkson, as he provided 24 points, five rebounds and two assists off the bench. Rodney Hood led the starters with 16 points, two rebounds and two assists. Collin Sexton finished with 16 points, five rebounds and four assists. Tristan Thompson amassed 11 points, 21 rebounds and five assists while Larry Nance Jr. totaled seven points and 12 boards. On deck for Cleveland is a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Wednesday. That will be their final game of the week, as Charlotte returns to action on Saturday when they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 109 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. Despite the fact that Cleveland led late in this game, Los Angeles was able to prevail with victory. In fact, the Cavaliers led 99 - 91 with less than five minutes remaining, as the Lakers ended the game on an 18 - 6 run. There were 13 ties and 20 lead changes in total though, as neither club led by more than 11 points.The shooting disparity really decided the game, with Los Angeles connecting on 51 percent of their shots while holding Cleveland to just 38 percent from the field. The Lakers also won the defensive rebounding battle, 44 - 31, and out - blocked them, 9 - 2. The Lakers (10 - 7) got a spectacular performance from LeBron James in his return to Cleveland, as he collected 32 points, 14 rebounds and seven assists. Lonzo Ball had one of his best game of the season, accumulating 15 points, seven rebounds and six assists on 7 - of - 11 shooting. Brandon Ingram finished with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. JaVale McGee and Kyle Kuzma scored 12 points apiece to round out the starting five. The Cavaliers (2 - 14) best player came off the bench, as Jordan Clarkson totaled 20 points, two rebounds and five assists against his former team. Tristan Thompson was the best starter, as he amassed 14 points and 15 boards. Cedi Osman accrued 21 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Collin Sexton generated 12 points, three rebounds and two assists. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Cleveland traveling to face the Philadelphia 76ers and Los Angeles playing host to the Utah Jazz in the nightcap.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 117 - 108, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday. Recent results would indicate an easy win for Houston but Cleveland actually prevailed in dominating fashion. In fact, they held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as they outscored the Rockets, 64 - 53, in the second and third quarters. The first half was extremely competitive though, as there were 12 lead changes in the first 20 minutes. Rebounding was the difference for the Cavaliers. as they outrebounded the Rockets, 49 - 30. Much of that came on the offensive end, with Cleveland winning that battle, 20 - 7. The Cavaliers also did some damage as ballhawks, as they recorded 11 steals while committing just 13 turnovers. The Rockets (9 - 9) decided to rest Chris Paul, as that clearly hurt their depth. James Harden did all he could though, as he collected 40 points, four rebounds and 13 assists. Eric Gordon finished with 28 points, two rebounds and three steals. Clint Capela amassed 12 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and four blocks. No other player scored more than seven points. The Cavaliers (4 - 14) got a career - best 29 points out of Collin Sexton, as he also provided four rebounds and two assists on 14 - of - 21 from the field. Tristan Thompson totaled 16 points, 20 rebounds and four steals. Jordan Clarkson was a huge spark off the bench, providing 20 points, five rebounds and four assists. On deck for Cleveland is a home matchup versus the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday. As for Houston, they're off until Wednesday, when they play host to the Dallas Mavericks.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 102 - 95, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday evening. Both teams got out to a good start, as they went back and forth through the first quarter, before the Timberwolves emerged with a, 29 - 26, lead heading into the second. The Timberwolves made the most of their momentum, as they pushed to a 10 - point lead early in the quarter. The managed to hold the lead for the entirety of the quarter, and take a, 54 - 47, lead into halftime. The Timberwolves kept it up through the third quarter, but the Cavaliers did not go away, as they cut the deficit to just four, after outscoring the visitors, 24 - 21, in the quarter. However, the T-Wolves would not be had that easily, as they once again pushed their lead back to double digits early in the fourth, and held on down the stretch, to earn their third straight win. Robert Covington led Minnesota with 24 points, seven rebounds, two steals, two blocks and one assist, in 38 minutes. Karl-Anthony Towns tallied 21 points, 10 rebounds, one assist and one block, while Jeff Teague added 13 points, six assists, three blocks, two rebounds and one steal. The Timberwolves shot 46 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 26 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyle Korver led the Cavs with 22 points on 7 - of - 12 shooting, in 21 minutes off the bench. The Cavs (4 - 15) will look to bounce back as they take on the Thunder in OKC on Wednesday. The Timberwolves (10 - 11) play host to the Spurs on Wednesday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 106 - 95, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Raptors (20 - 4) received news earlier in the day that star point guard Kyle Lowry (back) wouldn't suit up, which meant that the rest of the starting five would need to pick up the scoring slack. Toronto scuffled some without Lowry in the first half, but they still forged a solid 47 - 40 halftime lead. However, the Cavaliers (4 - 18) hung around, getting as close as 82 - 75 with 9:9 remaining. The visitors managed to stay one step ahead though, leading to the double - digit road win. Despite being short - handed, the Raptors shot a solid 49 percent while limiting Cleveland to a 39 percent success rate. Kawhi Leonard took the Raptors on his shoulders in Lowry's absence, leading the way with 34 points and adding nine rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. Danny Green supplied 15 points, seven rebounds and two blocks. Fred VanVleet drew the start for Lowry and also posted 15 points, adding four assists, three rebounds and one steal. Pascal Siakam matched VanVleet's scoring total and also offered five rebounds and five assists. Serge Ibaka contributed 10 points and six boards. Tristan Thompson and Jordan Clarkson co - led the Cavaliers with 18 points apiece. Thompson added 19 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Clarkson hauled in two rebounds, dished out two assists and recorded one steal. Rodney Hood and Alec Burks followed with matching 13 - point tallies. Cedi Osman totaled 12 points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal. Collin Sexton registered 10 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Raptors head back home for a Monday night showdown with the Denver Nuggets, while the Cavaliers hit the road and face the Brooklyn Nets on Monday evening as well.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. The final scoreline makes this game look more lopsided than it actually was, as a 34 - 19 fourth quarter really sealed things for the Warriors. In fact, there were eight ties and 10 lead changes in the first three quarters, as neither club attained a double - digit lead. Golden State's offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 45 - of - 85 from the field and 18 - of - 34 from three - point range. They did that while holding the Cavaliers to 39 - of - 89 from the field and 11 - of - 32 from long range, The Warriors also controlled the interior, as they won the defensive rebounding differential, 37 - 29, while out - blocking the Cavaliers, 5 - 2. The Warriors (17 - 9) got a shooting display from Stephen Curry, as he collected 42 points, nine rebounds and seven assists on 9 - of - 14 from three - point range. Kevin Durant finished with 25 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists. Klay Thompson accrued 16 points, four rebounds and two assists. Cedi Osman amassed 16 points, three rebounds and two steals. Tristan Thompson tallied 14 points and 19 boards. Jordan Clarkson led the bench with 17 points and three assists. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Golden State traveling to face the Milwaukee Bucks and Cleveland playing host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 110, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday evening. The Kings jumped out to a great start on the road, as they poured in 38 points in the first quarter, while holding the Cavs to 27 points, to take an 11 - point advantage into the second. The Cavs answered back in the second quarter, as they returned the favor by outscoring the visitors by 11 in the quarter, to make it a tie game at 66 by halftime. The Kings went back to work in the third quarter, as they quickly opened up a nine - point lead, and held on to outscore the Cavs, 30 - 23, to take a, 96 - 89, lead entering the final frame. The Kings kept the pressure on and pushed their lead to 15, early in the quarter. They were able to hold on from their to earn their third win in a row. De'Aaron Fox led Sacramento with 30 points, 12 assists, three steals and two rebounds, in 29 minutes. Buddy Hield added 25 points, four rebounds, two assists and two blocks, while Marvin Bagley III chipped in 17 points on 8 - of - 9 shooting, in 25 minutes off the bench. The Kings shot 58 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, despite having three players top 20 points, the Cavs still came up short at home. Jordan Clarkson was the high - point man, with 26 points on 11 - of - 19 shooting, in 29 minutes off the bench. Collin Sexton tallied 23 points, while Alec Burks added 22 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal, in 37 minutes off the bench. The Cavs (5 - 20) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Wizards on Saturday. The Kings (13 - 11) head to Indiana to take on the Pacers on Saturday.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Washington Wizards, 116 - 101, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Cavaliers (6 - 20) got a quick jump on the visiting Wizards (11 - 15), taking a 38 - 25 first - quarter lead. They were able to add a total of eight more points to their edge over the second and third periods, setting up a comfortable home win. Cleveland used a blend of impressive shooting (53 percent, including 48 percent from three - point range), a big 49 - 33 advantage on the boards and excellent ball security (seven turnovers) to secure victory. Six Cavaliers players hit double digits in the scoring column as well. Bradley Beal led the way for the Wizards with 27 points, a total he supplemented with five assists, four rebounds and one steal. Jeff Green poured in 17 points. Otto Porter, Jr. provided 15 points, seven rebounds, two assists and one steal. Kelly Oubre, Jr. registered 13 points, four rebounds and two assists. Markieff Morris mustered 11 points and added four rebounds and two assists. John Wall took the court despite an illness but managed just a single point while adding six assists and four rebounds over 26 minutes. Collin Sexton paced the Cavaliers with 29 points and added six assists, three rebounds and two steals. Tristan Thompson generated a 23 - point, 19 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and two blocks. Alec Burks drew the start for Rodney Hood and managed 14 points, seven rebounds, four assists and one steal. Larry Nance, Jr. totaled 13 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block. Cedi Osman and Jalen Jones had 12 points apiece. The Wizards remain on the road and take on the Indiana Pacers on Monday night, while the Cavaliers pay a visit to the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday evening as well.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the New York Knicks, 113 - 106, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday evening. The Cavaliers (7 - 21) and Knicks (8 - 21) demonstrated that their records are almost identical for good reason, as they engaged in an entertaining back - and - forth battle. Cleveland jumped out to a 39 - 26 first - quarter lead, but New York erased that deficit and then some by outscoring their hosts by a 63 - 47 margin over the middle periods. That set up a thrilling fourth quarter, one that saw the Knicks take a 106 - 105 lead with just 32 seconds remaining. However, an 80 run by the Cavs sealed the win, with Rodney Hood, Cedi Osman, Matthew Dellavedova and David Nwaba all contributing. Enes Kanter and Tim Hardaway, Jr. co - led the Knicks with 20 points apiece. Kanter added 10 rebounds and three assists, while Hardaway brought in five boards, dished out one assist and recorded both a steal and a block. Frank Ntilikina matched Mudiay's scoring total off the bench. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 28 points off the bench, a total he supplemented with five rebounds and two assists. Matthew Dellavedova enjoyed a successful return to Cleveland, posting 15 points, four rebounds, three assists and a steal. The Knicks remain on the road and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Friday night, while the Cavaliers remain home and take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday evening as well.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 114 - 102, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday evening. The Bucks (19 - 9) were looking to right the ship after a 16 - point loss to the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night. Milwaukee got off to a good start in that regard by taking a 27 - 16 first - quarter lead, which they'd extended to a 61 - 47 by halftime. That allowed them to essentially tread water in the second half and secure a double - digit win, despite missing both Malcolm Brogdon (hamstring) and Khris Middleton (finger). Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way for Milwaukee with 44 points, a total he supplemented with 14 rebounds and eight assists. Brook Lopez provided 19 points, five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Eric Bledsoe went for 16 points, six assists, five rebounds and one block. Ersan Ilyasova led the bench with 11 points and added four rebounds. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 23 points and added five rebounds, four assists and two steals. Rodney Hood poured in 19 points. Larry Nance, Jr. produced a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included six assists, three steals and one block. Alec Burks managed 12 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. Matthew Dellavedova had 10 points off the bench. The Bucks will next visit the Detroit Pistons on Monday night, while the Cavaliers remain home to take on the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday afternoon.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 128 - 105, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday evening. The two teams each enjoyed a dominant quarter in the first half, and the 76ers (20 - 11) forged a 65 - 58 halftime lead. The Cavaliers (7 - 23) were able to close the gap by another three points in the third, but Philadelphia put any thoughts of a Cleveland comeback to rest by racking up 39 points in the fourth quarter while limiting their hosts to 20. The Sixers were especially impressive in both shooting and on the boards, draining 56 percent of their attempts while outrebounding the Cavaliers by a 48 - 33 margin. Joel Embiid paced the Sixers with 24 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. Ben SImmons provided 22 points, 14 assists, 11 rebounds and one steal. Jimmy Butler returned to action and posted 19 points, two rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Landry Shamet led the bench with 16 points. J.J. Redick poured in 14 points and added four assists and three rebounds. Wilson Chandler filled out the stat sheet with 11 points, seven rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Cedi Osman and Jordan Clarkson generated matching 18 - point efforts to lead the Cavaliers. Osman added four rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Clarkson supplied six boards and dished out four assists. Rodney Hood and Matthew Dellavedova turned in 13 points apiece. Collin Sexton managed 12 points, two assists, one rebound and two steals. The 76ers continue on the road and take on the San Antonio Spurs on Monday night, while the Cavaliers pay a visit to the Indiana Pacers on Tuesday evening.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 112 - 92, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday. It's rare to see home teams thoroughly dominated in the NBA but that's just what Chicago did here in Cleveland. They did most of their damage in the second half, outscoring Cleveland, 58 - 33. There were actually 18 lead changes in the first 30 minutes of action, as that 30 - 15 third quarter really made the difference. That allowed the Bulls to shoot 55 percent from the field and 50 percent from three - point range while holding the Cavaliers to 45 percent from the field and 30 percent from long range. The Cavaliers (8 - 26) were led by Larry Nance Jr. as he accrued 20 points, six rebounds and three steals. Cedi Osman totaled 17 points and seven boards. Alex Burks started and provided 12 points, six rebounds and three assists. Jordan Clarkson led their bench with 17 points, one rebound and one assist. The Bulls (9 - 25) were led by Lauri Markkanen, as he tallied 31 points, four rebounds and three assists. Kris Dunn accrued 17 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. Justin Holiday finished with 15 points, five rebounds and three steals. Ryan Arcidiacono totaled 12 points, four rebounds, eight assists and three steals. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Chicago playing host to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Cleveland traveling to face the Memphis Grizzlies.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 117 - 92, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. While Cleveland led for the majority of the first quarter, that's the only time they were in this game. In fact, Miami rode a 36 - 20 second quarter to victory, as they won each of the final three quarters by at least five points apiece. The Heat actually held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. The rebounding differential was obviously decisive, with Miami winning that battle, 47 - 22. Justise Winslow accrued 10 points, four rebounds and seven assists. Tyler Johnson led the bench with 16 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals. Cedi Osman collected 12 points, four rebounds and four assists. Larry Nance Jr. moved back to the bench, as he provided six points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Miami welcoming the struggling Washington Wizards to South Beach and Cleveland playing host to the Utah Jazz.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 117 - 91, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday night. The Cavaliers (8 - 30) came out ready to defend home court, as they forged a 49 - 48 halftime lead after a tightly contested first 24 minutes. Donovan Mitchell led the way for the Jazz with 18 points and added five assists and three rebounds. Jae Crowder had a bench - leading 16 points and also supplied five rebounds, two assists and one steal. Ricky Rubio posted 15 points, five assists and four rebounds. Joe Ingles and Rudy Gobert had 12 points apiece and also hauled in seven and nine rebounds, respectively. Derrick Favors and Kyle Korver contributed 10 points apiece. Alec Burks paced the Cavaliers with 17 points, adding three rebounds, two assists and one block. Collin Sexton managed 13 points, three assists, one rebound and one steal. Cedi Osman and Tristan Thompson generated eight points apiece, with Thompson notably pulling down 12 rebounds as well. The Jazz next pay a visit to the Detroit Pistons on Saturday night, while the Cavaliers remain home to face the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday evening as well.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 133 - 98, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. Jahlil Okafor and E'Twaun Moore generated 10 points apiece. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 23 points and added four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Tristan Thompson managed a 10 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two steals and one block. The Pelicans head back home to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night, while the Cavaliers remain home to tangle with the Indiana Pacers on Tuesday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 123 - 115, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Pacers would end up losing the remaining three quarters (25 - 27, 29 - 36 and 31 - 36, respectively) but it wasn't enough since Cleveland were never able to come back from such a huge deficit following the first 12 minutes of action. The Chicago Bulls defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 104 - 88, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday afternoon. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Washington Wizards, 116 - 113, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Boston Celtics defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 103 - 96, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 107 - 104, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday. In a battle between the two worst teams in the NBA, it came down to the final shot. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers in triple overtime, 148 - 139, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday evening. The Nets (30 - 29) and Cavaliers (12 - 46) had both been involved in their fair share of shootouts this season, but what unfolded Wednesday ended up being on another level altogether. Most of regulation hinted at what was to come in the latter stages, as the game was a back - and - forth affair for the majority of the first four quarters. Cleveland had pulled ahead by as much as five points with under four minutes to go in the final period before Brooklyn fought back and ultimately sent the game into the first overtime on a D'Angelo Russell driving layup with 1:1 remaining. Collin Sexton returned the favor for the hosts at the end of the first extra period with 3 seconds left to force a sixth quarter. At the end of the second overtime, it was DeMarre Carroll making up for missing a floater at the end of regulation by hitting a 26 - foot step back jumper at the buzzer to knot the score back up at 128. The visitors finally got the best of the exhausted Cavs in the third overtime, outscoring them by a 20 - 11 margin and finishing on a 7 - 2 run over the final 1:5 to secure the win. Russell overcame a forgettable start to lead the way for the Nets with 36 points. He added eight assists and seven rebounds. Joe Harris netted 25 points and also contributed four rebounds and two assists. Carroll offered 18 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one block. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson delivered 17 points, five rebounds and one steal. Allen Crabbe supplied 14 points and seven boards, while Caris LeVert turned in 12 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and one block. Jarrett Allen and Shabazz Napier had matching 10 - point tallies while also compiling 12 rebounds and seven assists, respectively. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 42 points and complemented them with eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Sexton managed 24 points, six boards and five assists. Marquese Chriss registered 23 points, seven boards, one assist and two steals. Cedi Osman returned from injury to offer 13 points, five rebounds and three assists. Larry Nance, Jr. mustered eight points and 14 rebounds. The Nets are now off until Feb. 21, when they'll host the Portland Trail Blazers. The Cavaliers return to action that same evening and host the Phoenix Suns.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 111 - 98, at Quicken Loans Arena on Thursday. The Suns (11 - 49) and the Cavaliers (13 - 46) have been two of the worst teams in The Association this season, so the stakes weren't very high for this game to begin with. Phoenix got on top, though, since they jumped to a 28 - 23 following the first quarter, but that was the only lead they would have during the rest of the contest. Cleveland quickly turned things around and they jumped to a four - point lead at the break (55 - 51) thanks to a 32 - 23 second quarter. Cleveland would never look back afterwards, though. Cleveland would win the remaining two quarters (22 - 21 and 34 - 26, respectively) and they ended winning the contest by a higher - than - expected 13 - point margin. DeAndre Ayton contributed 13 points and nine rebounds, while Josh Jackson chipped in with 12 points and six boards. Richaun Holmes had six points and five boards coming off the bench.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 112 - 107, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday evening. The Cavs got out to a great start at home, with a 37 - 24 lead after one quarter. The Grizzlies pushed back in the second, where they outscored the Cavs by six, to cut the deficit to seven by halftime. The score went back and forth, until the Cavs created some separation in the final minutes with a couple of big plays from Collin Sexton and Cedi Osman. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 123 - 110, at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday evening. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 129 - 93, at Quicken Loans Arena on Saturday afternoon. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 107 - 93, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Toronto Raptors at Quicken Loans Arena on Monday night. The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 107 - 102, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday evening. The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Cleveland, Cavaliers, 110 - 108, at Quicken Loans Arena on Friday. This game meant a lot more to Los Angeles than Cleveland but the Cavaliers left it all on the floor in this competitive battle. A 40 - 25 first quarter got the Cavaliers out to a big lead but Los Angeles responded by outscoring them in the middle quarters, 67 - 43. That allowed the Clippers to hold the lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Free-throw shooting was huge, with Los Angeles hitting 20 - of - 23 and Cleveland connecting on just 10 - of - 13. Ball movement was also critical, with the Clippers out - assisting the Cavaliers, 24 - 14. The Clippers (43 - 30) were led by Danilo Gallinari, as he tallied 27 points, three rebounds and three assists. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander totaled 16 points, two rebounds, five assists and two steals. Landry Shamet started and amassed 13 points and seven boards. Lou Williams led the bench with 15 points, two rebounds and six assists. The Cavaliers (19 - 54) were led by Kevin Love, as he tallied 22 points and eight rebounds. Collin Sexton finished with 20 points and four boards. Cedi Osman generated 11 points, two rebounds and three assists while Jordan Clarkson led the bench with 20 points, five rebounds and two assists. Larry Nance Jr. provided 14 points, nine rebounds and three steals off the bench as well. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Los Angeles traveling to face the New York Knicks and Cleveland playing the Milwaukee Bucks on the road as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the host Cleveland Cavaliers, 116 - 106, at Quicken Loans Arena on Wednesday. Boston came into this game as a sizable favorite, as they led for all but a few minutes. In fact, they won all four individual quarters, despite the fact that each one was decided by five points or fewer. Rebounding was the difference in the game, with the Celtics out - rebounding the Cavaliers, 46 - 36. Their defense was key as well, as they doubled up Cleveland in steals, 8 - 4 and tripled them up in blocks, 3 - 1, while winning the turnover differential, 15 - 10. The Celtics (44 - 31) were led by Jayson Tatum, as he tallied 21 points, five rebounds and four assists. Marcus Smart matched those 21 points, adding six rebounds, four assists and three steals to his tally. Al Horford accrued 19 points, eight rebounds and five assists while Gordon Hayward led the bench with 15 points, five rebounds and four assists. The Cavaliers (19 - 56) were led by Collin Sexton, as he amassed 24 points, two rebounds and three assists. Cedi Osman accumulated 15 points, seven rebounds and two assists, Kevin Love finished with 10 points, 11 rebounds and four assists while Jordan Clarkson led the bench with 18 points, two rebounds and five assists. On deck for the Cavaliers is a road matchup versus the San Antonio Spurs on Thursday. As for the Celtics, they return to action on Friday when they play host to the Indiana Pacers.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 112 - 90, at Quicken Loans Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Spurs (47 - 34) came into the contest looking to continue sharpening up their collective game for the forthcoming postseason. However, the Cavaliers (19 - 62) had the mentality of spoiler early, matching the visitors bucket for bucket during the first quarter. San Antonio then kicked it into gear in the second forging a 16 - point lead by halftime with a 38 - point second period. After a third period where both defenses shined and only 34 combined points were scored, the Spurs finished Cleveland off by adding another six points to their advantage. San Antonio dominated on both the scoreboard and the glass, shooting 52 percent while winning the battle of the boards by a 49 - 34 margin. LaMarcus Aldridge paced the Spurs with 18 points, adding 13 rebounds, two assists and one steal. DeMar DeRozan, Davis Bertans and Patty Mills generated matching 14 - point efforts. DeRozan also dished out nine assists. Bryn Forbes finished with 13 points, six rebounds and four assists. Jakob Poeltl managed eight points but also hauled in 10 rebounds and recorded a pair of blocks and steals apiece. Collin Sexton and Brandon Knight co - led the Cavaliers with 16 points. Ante Zizic followed with 14 points, six rebounds and two assists. Cedi Osman furnished 12 points, four boards and two steals. Larry Nance, Jr. generated an 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and four steals. The Spurs head back home to face the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night, while the Cavaliers remain home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday evening.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 124 - 97, at Quicken Loans Arena on Tuesday. The Hornets (39 - 42) had their backs against the wall in this game against the Cavaliers (19 - 63), who were simply looking to end the year as soon as possible, and Charlotte got the job done as they needed a win - - as well as other results - - to keep their playoff chances alive on Wednesday. The Hornets didn't waste any time and jumped to a 33 - 31 lead in the first half and they would blow the game open the rest of the way. Charlotte won every single quarter in this contest (with the others being 31 - 25, 26 - 19 and 34 - 22) to secure a huge 27 - point win. They never stepped the foot out of the gas, but that was expected given their situation on the standings. Kemba Walker led the way for the Hornets since he finished with 23 points and seven assists in only 27 minutes of action. Miles Bridges filled the stat sheet with 18 points, seven rebounds and four assists, while Dwayne Bacon chipped in with 18 points, Jeremy Lamb had an impressive effort off the bench with 23 points and five assists, while Frank Kaminsky (14 points) and Devonte Graham (10 points) also scored in double digits. Colllin Sexton led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points and 10 assists, while Cedi Osman contributed 17 points and four rebounds. Larry Nance Jr. filled the stat sheet admirably since he ended with 10 points, 12 boards, six assists and two blocks. Jordan Clarkson chipped in with 16 points in 23 minutes off the bench, while Channing Frye ended with 10 points.
